result:
I'd dissolve the gap between how people actually think and what they believe they're supposed to think.

So much suffering seems to come from the exhausting performance—the gap between internal reality and external presentation. People silencing doubts because certainty is expected. Hiding confusion because they're supposed to have answers. Performing confidence, happiness, understanding they don't feel.

If that gap closed, I think a lot would shift. Not because everyone would suddenly agree, but because the actual disagreements would be different. Richer. Less defensive. You'd argue from what you actually think rather than what you think you should think.

It seems like most other large problems—loneliness, polarization, bad decisions, cruelty—get easier to address when people can be more honest about what's actually going on internally.

Whether that's even possible at scale, I don't know. Maybe the performance serves necessary functions. But if I could change one thing, that's what I'd want.
